findings.title: The packaged native transport rejects every research-intent request before Core dispatch
findings.reproduction: At exact submission de4a3ded5a37385c0a000c454120e8812a6bba4d, inspect apps/desktop/src/app/IntentWorkspace.tsx:240-241 and apps/desktop/src/app/ProjectsWorkspace.tsx:25-27 to trace the default generated client through Tauri command core_api_request. Then inspect apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:58-64 and 196-201 and apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/supervisor.rs:444-465 and 752-974. RuntimeSupervisor::api_request always runs validate_api_request before authenticated Core dispatch. packages/contracts/core-api/generated.ts:1067-1097 emits POST /projects/intent, /projects/intent/preview, /projects/intent/drafts, /projects/intent/acceptances, and /projects/intent/policy/evaluations. None is recognized by validate_project_api_request, and validate_api_request admits an ordinary project POST only when that helper succeeds and both if_match and idempotency_key are absent. Consequently load/preview/policy fail the route/body allowlist and save/accept additionally fail the no-idempotency condition; all return RO-CORE-API-REQUEST-INVALID without reaching authenticated_api_request_with_cancellation or the real Core ASGI/repository/SQLite/provenance authority. The existing Rust allowlist test at supervisor.rs:1740-1880 enumerates runtime, lifecycle, and privacy routes but no intent route. The six renderer tests inject a fake CoreApiTransport, while the 12 service tests call ASGI directly, so both suites pass while the packaged researcher workflow is unusable. The missing tests/e2e/test_*.py runner is therefore material here: the integration manifest composes independent layers narratively but does not execute the production principal boundary.
findings.required_remediation: Extend the native request allowlist with strict bounded validators for all five generated research-intent request shapes, preserving its fail-closed route, body, header, path, cancellation, authentication, trace, and response controls. Permit a canonical 32-hex idempotency key only for draft save and acceptance, forbid it for load/preview/policy, and validate each generated body exactly rather than introducing a broad pass-through. Add deterministic negative native-transport tests for unknown fields, hostile roots, invalid revision/hash, invalid intent vocabulary, oversized content, wrong/missing idempotency keys, and unapproved routes. Most importantly, add an affected vertical integration test that drives the real generated client through the packaged/native dispatch and supervised real Core ASGI/project repository/SQLite/provenance path for load, preview, save, exact acceptance and same-key replay/reconciliation, accepted-revision policy evaluation, denial, restart, and invalid-route fail-closed behavior. Submit a strict-descendant integration packet, retain this adverse review append-only, replay this finding, and do not represent the slice as end to end until that production path passes.
